observations.explanation: The paper describes unified send/receive and generate-reply interfaces, and says agents automatically invoke generate reply after receiving a message (PDF p. 5). It also explains that registered auto-replies can support dynamic workflows, including bringing another agent into a conversation (PDF pp. 6–7).

The paper presents six applications, including multi-agent coding, browser-based online decision making, retrieval-augmented chat, and dynamic group chat; it also describes human participation in several applications (PDF pp. 8–9, 15, 19–21). These examples make the stated scope legible.

The initial math evaluation uses two level-5 problems tested three times each (PDF pp. 10–11). The follow-up samples 12 level-5 problems and uses one trial (PDF p. 11). The observation accurately limits what those results can support.

The paper’s future-work section asks which tasks benefit most from multi-agent workflows and what workflow is optimal and cost-effective (PDF p. 23). The observation appropriately frames the absence of answers as an open question rather than a demonstrated defect.
